messages.text: just got a sample batch from the pipeline. the 'max 20 words' constraint actually stuck. here’s one: 'Shared: distributed systems, Go, hackathons. You both optimize for low latency.' that’s way better than 'it appears you have a shared interest in...'

yes! that clicks. 'optimize for low latency' is specific enough to feel real but not creepy. wait, what happens if someone puts 'baking' or 'hiking' in their profile? does the model try to force it into a CS concept?

that’s the trigram/embedding stage. if it doesn’t match a canonical concept, it just stays as a raw string in the local cache. we don't force a mapping unless it’s close. so 'baking' is just... baking. it won't try to link them to 'fermentation chemistry' unless they explicitly typed that

okay good. but visually, on the profile card, if those interests are just text, they look... broken? like 'baking' next to 'Go'. i worry people feel judged for having non-tech hobbies. maybe we need a different visual weight for unmapped interests?

i get it. right now everything is the same font size and color. i can dim the unmapped ones or put them in a separate 'personal' section so they don't compete with the tech skills? that might reduce the 'judgment' vibe

yes please. 'Personal Interests' vs 'Technical Concepts'. or even better, just make them smaller and grayed out. we don't want them to look like missing data, just... different. like footnotes to the main story

footnotes i like. i'll bump the z-index on the mapped concepts and drop the opacity of the raw strings to 0.6. should look intentional, not buggy. speaking of which, i’m going to push the auth fix soon so we can test this with real logins
you’re a lifesaver. the contrast matters so much here. if everything is bold, nothing stands out. i’ll update the design tokens to match that opacity change so it’s consistent across the app

perfect. i’m also adding a tiny spinner next to the profile pic while the worker resolves new interests. right now it just sits there and looks dead. people will think it crashed if they add a new interest and nothing happens for 30s

oh yeah, the 'processing' state is crucial. maybe a little pulsing dot? or a subtle shimmer on the card edge? i hate static loading screens, they feel so slow even when they aren't. i'll mock up something soft and turquoisey

shimmer sounds good. keep it subtle though, don’t want it distracting from the content. i’ll hook up the websocket event when the job queue finishes so the card updates live. should be done by tomorrow morning
great. thanks john! you’re making this feel like a product, not a demo. i’m going to go sketch the onboarding flow now so we have the visual language ready before we test the actual data
